messages.text: Zheng stuns Andreeva to become first Chinese winner of China Open

metadata.summary: Olympic champion Qinwen Zheng made history as the ‌first Chinese player to win the China Open on Sunday, stunning French ‌Open winner Mirra Andreeva 7-5 6-4.
metadata.content: China Open: Qinwen Zheng stuns Mirra Andreeva to make history as first Chinese winner of WTA event in Beijing | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to main content China Open: Qinwen Zheng stuns Mirra Andreeva to make history as first Chinese winner of WTA event in Beijing Sunday's WTA China Open final sees home favourite Qinwen Zheng make history as the first-ever Chinese winner, defeating 2026 French Open champion Mirra Zndreeva with superb display; You can watch ATP 1000 Shanghai Masters from October 7-18 live on Sky Sports Tennis Sunday 11 October 2026 14:59, UK Image: Zheng Qinwen created tennis history on Sunday as she became the first Chinese player ever to clinch the China Open title Olympic champion Qinwen Zheng made history as the ‌first Chinese player to win the China Open on Sunday, stunning French ‌Open winner Mirra Andreeva 7-5 6-4. Wild card ​Zheng, who has been on a recovery path after missing nearly six ​months due to an elbow ‌injury on her dominant right arm, looked like her ​old self as she used powerful forehands to control the rallies, and landed swift ​winners angling away from Andreeva. After ⁠the two exchanged early ⁠breaks, world No 5 Andreeva held firm to go 5-4 ‌up, and almost got a decisive break when Zheng sent a cross-court shot too ‌long before netting a forehand. messages.text: Yamashita wins Korea Championship with course-record finish

metadata.summary: Miyu Yamashita put on a show on the final day of the LET's Aramco Korea Championship, firing a course record of 63 (-9) to win by three strokes with a total of 22 under par.
metadata.content: Aramco Korea Championship: Miyu Yamashita produces course-record finish to clinch Ladies European Tour title | Golf News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Aramco Korea Championship: Miyu Yamashita produces course-record finish to clinch Ladies European Tour title Ladies European Tour's Aramco Korea Championship sees Japan's Miyu Yamashita produce course record on final day to clinch title ahead of Czech Republic's Sara Kouskova; title is Yamashita's second title on LET, having also won the 2025 AIG Women's Open Sunday 11 October 2026 11:35, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the final round of the Aramco Korea Championship Miyu Yamashita put on a show on the final day of the LET's Aramco Korea Championship, firing a course record of 63 (-9) to win by three strokes with a total of 22 under par. The world No 5 led from the 36-hole mark and was bogey-free once again at New Korea Country Club. Yamashita began well with birdies on the third, fifth, eighth and 10th holes to put herself in a good position with seven holes to go. However, the Czech Republic's Sara Kouskova was hot on her heels, but the 25-year-old major champion rolled in three birdies in four holes before making an eagle on 17 to seal her fourth win of 2026. It was the Japanese star's second title on the Ladies European Tour (LET), having also won the 2025 AIG Women's Open. messages.text: Brennan holds on for one-shot victory at Baycurrent Classic in Japan

metadata.summary: Michael Brennan won the Baycurrent Classic for his second victory of the season and third on the PGA Tour, parring the final six holes for a three-under 68 and a one-stroke margin over Jacob Bridgeman and Keith Mitchell.
metadata.content: Baycurrent Classic: Michael Brennan holds on to win title in Japan ahead of Jacob Bridgeman and Keith Mitchell | Golf News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Baycurrent Classic: Michael Brennan holds on to win title in Japan ahead of Jacob Bridgeman and Keith Mitchell American Michael Brennan holds off challenges of compatriots Jacob Bridgeman and Keith Mitchell to clinch PGA Tour's Baycurrent Classic in Japan with victory; Win is Brennan's second title of season and third in his career; England's Jordan Smith finished three shots off the top Sunday 11 October 2026 08:45, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the final round of the PGA Tour Baycurrent Classic Michael Brennan won the Baycurrent Classic for his second victory of the season and third on the PGA Tour, parring the final six holes for a three-under 68 and a one-stroke margin over Jacob Bridgeman and Keith Mitchell. Tied for the third-round lead with Bridgeman and Zach Bauchou in the FedEx Cup Fall event, Brennan rebounded from a bogey on the 10th with birdies on holes 11 and 12 before the winning par run at hilly Yokohama Country Club. His best par save came on the par-3 16th when he hit a long shot from a greenside bunker to a foot. He finished at 16-under 268. Why were his side outplayed at home by the Premier League's bottom club? Why can't they hold onto leads? Why do they seem incapable of playing against 10 men?
